sentences.text: A chart can only show what fits on paper.
It can’t tell you that the inlet shoals after a blow, that the bridge opens on the half hour, or where to find fuel.
For that, a captain keeps a small library, and today I’ll walk you along the shelf.
The United States Coast Pilot is published by NOAA, and it holds what the chart can’t show.
Navigation regulations, local hazards, anchorages, bridge and cable clearances, currents, weather, and descriptions of ports and channels.
Coast Pilot four covers the Atlantic coast, from Cape Henry in Virginia down to Key West.
Coast Pilot five covers the Gulf coast, Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands.
So a captain working out of Tampa Bay needs which one?
And it’s free to download, and updated regularly.
Before you run any inlet for the first time, read its page.
